author: David Jarboe (Country Boy Computers)
method_caveats: Self-published spreadsheet embedded in the page; llama.cpp llama-bench style columns pp512 (prompt tok/s) and tg128 (generation tok/s), 32k n_ctx.
The page does not say how many cards each row used. Qwen3-Coder-Next Q4 (80B) is ~48 GB of weights, so that row cannot be a single 32 GB card; treat card count as unknown.
Author notes flash attention was off on all Navi (V620) tests because of a ROCm bug.
These are one person's numbers on his machines. Not reproduced by us.

rows.note: Prefill ~50 and generation ~45 tok/s; 24-30 tok/s when the 96k context was 80% full (Lon Seidman).
~32 tok/s generation, 133-160 tok/s prompt, 128k context. Draw is his highest seen on the V100.

reader_reports.claim: Dell workstation would not POST with two 32GB V620s until MMIO high granularity was raised from 1GB to 64GB chunks via the UEFI shell; BIOS UI did not expose it.
Speculative decoding on Qwen 3.8 27B (llama.cpp, 2x V620) raised generation from 19 to 40 tok/s.

image_video_notes: Lon Seidman: Flux 1024x1024 ~1 min; LTX 2.5 5s 720p ~3.5 min; MiniMax H3 too slow on V100. Intel Arc card was under 1.5 min on the same job.

system_comparisons.title: Apple Mac Studio 512 GB (1 unit) vs ASUS Ascent GX10 128 GB (4 units)
system_comparisons.author: X post
system_comparisons.model: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, original weights, same bench on both
method_caveats: One poster's numbers, not reproduced by us. Reader report, not verified.

The post names the runners as mlx-serve on the Mac and spark-ds41f on the GX10 units. It does not state versions or flags. Quantization details beyond "original weights", and power draw, were not stated.
Text and code are separate workloads, as the post reports them.
The post mentions DGX Spark recipes. The shortened link in the post is the attached photo, and that link was not followed.
The prices are the figures written in the post, not a store listing checked by us. The post says ASUS GX10 and groups the four units with DGX Spark.
The post text was read through a public status mirror on 2026-11-12 because x.com returned 403. The numbers match that text.
